newsitem.title: USA: USWC distillates hold on ARCO rumor, gasoline dips.
newsitem.headline: USWC distillates hold on ARCO rumor, gasoline dips.

text.p: U.S. West Coast distillates held firm despite weaker spot gasoline prices Wedneday, finding support in rumors that ARCO's diesel output continued to fall short in Los Angeles, traders said.

Prices at L.A. loading terminals (racks), a market derived from wholesales prices, rose two cents late last week to around 86 cents a gallon. Despite ARCO denials, traders speculated a hydrocracking or hydrotreating unit had a mechanical failure.
"(Racks) have been up a couple cents. It would only be a mechanical problem," one broker said.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles rose one cent from Tuesday to 78.50/79.50 cents, while conventional grade was steady at 67.50/68.50 cents.
But gasoline values sagged amid signs of stable production in the region.

Tosco and its oil worker union averted a strike by agreeing to a labor contract this weekend, and the end of maintenance season saw California refineries throttle up their output, according to traders and industry reports.

West Coast gasoline stocks gained 98,000 barrels as of March 28, while refinery utilization was nearly unchanged at 89.8 percent of capacity, according to a weekly report published by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Los Angeles CARB was talked 3.50 cents a gallon lower in early trade, with offers seen at 79 cents.
